title: Performance Ratio (PR%) Definition and Calculation
summary: Performance Ratio (PR%) is the definitive international metric comparing actual net AC output to theoretical STC output from measured plane-of-array sunlight.
content: Defined by standard IEC 61724, Performance Ratio (PR%) is the ratio of actual AC energy generated by the solar plant to the theoretical energy the plant would have generated if operating continuously at its rated STC efficiency under measured plane-of-array irradiance: PR = (E_ac / P_stc) / (H_poa / G_stc), where E_ac is actual energy (kWh), P_stc is rated DC capacity (kWp), H_poa is measured plane-of-array insolation (kWh/m²), and G_stc is 1000 W/m². A well-designed, unshaded rooftop solar installation in a temperate climate typically achieves a PR between 78% and 86%. PR accounts for all systemic losses (inverter conversion, wiring resistance, thermal derating, and module soiling).

title: Actual versus Expected Generation Discrepancies
summary: Analyzing the percentage variance between real-time inverter generation and meteorological physics expectations isolates system faults from weather effects.
content: To accurately detect solar anomalies, SolarBuddy compares actual inverter telemetry with predicted generation calculated by physical atmospheric and irradiance models. The generation difference is calculated as: Difference (%) = ((Actual - Expected) / Expected) * 100. Discrepancy classifications: 1) Normal Variance (-10% to +10%): Natural atmospheric fluctuations, transient cloud fringes, or slight measurement variance; 2) Mild Underperformance (-15% to -25%): Often indicates surface soiling/dust accumulation or elevated ambient temperatures; 3) Severe Deficit (-50% to -95%): Indicates string open circuit, disconnected MPPT channel, tripped breaker, or extensive obstruction; 4) Zero Generation (-100%): Complete system outage, tripped main AC breaker, or grid lockout.

title: System Loss Budget and Derating Factors
summary: The cumulative loss budget includes DC wiring, inverter conversion, shading, soiling, and light reflection factors.
content: A photovoltaic system experiences multiple sequential loss mechanisms before electricity reaches the grid: 1) Soiling Loss (typically 2.0%–5.0% depending on rainfall and maintenance); 2) DC Wiring Loss (I²R resistive losses in DC cables, typically 1.5%–2.5%); 3) AC Cable Loss (typically 1.0%–1.5%); 4) Inverter Conversion Loss (typically 1.5%–2.5%); 5) Shading Derate (unshaded installations operate at 0.95–1.00); 6) Module Mismatch (manufacturing tolerance variance between series-connected panels, typically 1.0%–1.5%). The total compound derating factor is calculated by multiplying each sub-system transmission factor: F_total = ∏(1 - L_i).
